post.description: Snapshot each counted balance (qty + version). Nothing posts until a manager posts it.

Post variances as COUNT_ADJUSTMENT rows. If any balance moved since it was counted the
whole count is refused (STALE_COUNT) — recount rather than overwrite newer stock.
Move damaged stock out of a saleable lot into its DAMAGED companion lot (two rows).

Server-Sent Events: `stock` whenever committed inventory state changes (polls committed
state, so events are only ever emitted after commit). Clients reconnect on close.

get.description: The exact bytes stored at issue (never re-rendered), so the hash always matches.

Signed proof of delivery (raw file body). Kept unaltered next to the invoice; a second
different copy is added beside it, the same bytes again return the existing file (200).

get.description:
Line accuracy over accepted readings: a line counts as correct when the reviewer confirmed
it as read. Corrected, removed and manually added (missed) lines count as wrong.

post.description: Read (or re-read) a received scan. An unfinished earlier reading is superseded.

Every line reviewed → a DRAFT sales order (source SCAN, linked to the scan). Nothing else:
no reservation, no invoice, no stock movement.
A line the reading missed. Counted as a miss in accuracy.
Not an order (or unusable). The scan and the reading stay on file.

get.description:
Printable order sheet (template PT-OS-1) the customer fills in by hand; scans of it are
read line by line.

post.description: Not found at the bank (or wrong amount): the report is closed, never deleted.

Bank / cheque / receipt checked by an authorised employee. Optional allocations are
applied in the same transaction.

get.description: Warehouse queue. `code` matches the QR/printed pick code exactly.

schema.title: Response List Attempts Api V1 Pick Attempts Get

post.description:
Void a sheet that was never verified (e.g. lost/reprinted). Its quantities return to
pending; the record is kept.
Read-only draft: billed lines, totals and stock check. Nothing is numbered or posted.

Warehouse enters what was actually packed. 0 = `NO` (a shortage, not a cancellation);
anything below the request needs a shortage reason.
Verifier sends a submitted sheet back to the warehouse for correction.

SUBMITTED -> VERIFIED. Shortfalls stay pending (BACKORDER) unless the verifier, holding
sales_order.close, explicitly cancels them with a reason.
Validate a CSV and diff it against a version (default: current). Saves nothing.

get.description: Header plus one example row per active product/unit with the current rate (if any).

schema.title: Response List Versions Api V1 Price Books Versions Get

post.description: New draft, empty or cloned from `based_on_id` (default: the current price book).

Create a DRAFT from a full price book CSV. All-or-nothing; the same content uploaded
twice (any formatting/order) is rejected with 409 DUPLICATE_UPLOAD.

Approve a draft. It becomes immutable and takes effect at `effective_at` (default now).
Only new documents priced after that moment use it; issued documents keep their snapshot.
Cancel a scheduled (not yet effective) version. Effective history can't be archived.

get.description: Diff `version_id` against another version (default: current, else what it was based on).

post.description: Delete a DRAFT and its entries (published versions can never be deleted).

get.description: Alphabetical (product name, SKU, unit, scope) price grid with filters.

put.description: Set one rate in a DRAFT (insert or update by product/unit/scope/target).

get.description: Full version as an importable CSV (round-trips to the same content hash).
Price a product for a customer at a moment: customer > group > standard.
Exact normalized match; a source-specific alias wins over a generic one.

post.description:
Read-only computation (no idempotency needed). Conversions come only from this
product's active profiles; anything else is UNKNOWN_CONVERSION, never guessed.

get.description:
Aging of open invoices (warehouse-scoped by invoice.read) with confirmed-but-unapplied
and reported-but-unconfirmed payment totals per customer.
Posted GRNs per vendor and unit: declared vs accepted / damaged / rejected.

Totals of issued invoices in the period, quantities per unit and a per-day or per-month
series (every period present, zero when nothing was invoiced).

One row per product and unit. With `customer_id` it is that customer's volume and
average realised rate per product.

Opening + received + dispatched + other = closing, per product and unit, from the
stock ledger. Closing includes damaged and quarantined lots.

post.description: New DRAFT. The original request (text + per-line snapshot) is frozen here forever.

Cancel a whole order that has never been picked. Drafts: sales_order.manage;
confirmed orders: sales_order.close.

Close with shortage: every pending quantity is cancelled with the reason. Refused while
a pick is in progress or picked goods still await invoicing.

DRAFT -> CONFIRMED. Prices resolve now (customer > group > standard) and are frozen on
each line; later price books never change this order. No invoice number is assigned.
Cancel part of a line's pending quantity (e.g. customer no longer wants the backorder).
Issue a picking sheet for every line's pending quantity. One active sheet per order.
Device auth + valid capability for this job and device → SCANNING (single flight).
Scanner unplugged / driver missing / timeout → FAILED; the UI offers manual upload.
Scanned bytes for a job this device claimed. Retrying after success returns the job.

One-time: exchange the pairing code for a device secret. The bridge shows the
fingerprint on screen; the operator confirms it in the web app (approve).

get.description: Scanners the caller can use (scan.create/review) or manage.

schema.title: Response List Devices Api V1 Scan Devices Get

post.description: Creates a PENDING scanner and a one-time pairing code (shown once, stored hashed).
Second half of the handshake: the operator types the fingerprint the bridge displays.
Immediately invalidates the bridge secret; open jobs on it fail.

get.description: Original bytes, private. Allowed when the caller can read a scan that holds them.

post.description:
Ask a paired bridge to scan. Returns a single-use capability the browser hands to the
bridge on localhost; the bridge must present it to claim this job.

Manual fallback (always available). Raw file body. The same bytes uploaded again return
the existing scan (200, duplicate) instead of creating a second source record.

Capture freight/duty/etc. Allowed after posting too (bills arrive late). Never allocated
to lots automatically. Does not change the shipment's version once it is posted.
Record a physical count line (accepted / damaged / rejected). Not stock until posted.
Drop an unposted count line (a miscount). The audit log keeps what it said.

Record what a vendor document says. Never stock. If no product is chosen, the label is
matched against the vendor's remembered names, then SKUs/aliases/names company-wide.
Attach a document already brought in through the Scan Center (bridge or upload).

Upload a vendor document straight onto the shipment (raw file body). The bytes are kept
unaltered as a source document and also appear in the Scan Center as a vendor document.

Approve the GRN: accepted -> saleable stock, damaged -> damaged lot, rejected -> nothing.
Any difference from the documents must be acknowledged with a note. Exactly once.
Send a submitted count back for recounting (before posting only).
Counting finished: hand over for approval. Counting is frozen until reopened.
